Action 3: The OJK adopted the Digital Finance Innovation Road Map and Action Plan, 2020-2024, will establish the policy priorities in Fintech to support the government's financial inclusion strategies, including a specific focus on women. Action 4: Bank Indonesia: (i) launched Indonesia's Payment System Blueprint 2025 to reinforce the integration of the national digital economy and finance; and (ii) strengthened existing policy to increase the use of digital transactions by lowering National Clearing System transaction cost by 40% for banks, reducing the upper limit of fund transfer fee charged to consumers by 30%, and increasing the frequency of settlement cycles of fund transfer services from five times, and regular payment services from two times, to nine times a day. Base year: 2019 Base value: 76.19% (O), 75.15% (W) Target date: 2020-12-31 Target value: 92%
Action 5: The CMEA piloted the use of national biometric ID (Electronic Kartu Tanda Penduduk [e- KTP]) to facilitate electronic know-your-customer (e-KYC) to reduce the time and cost of opening an account while maintaining the highest degree of anti- money laundering (AML) and security standards. Base year: 2019 Base value: 76.19% (O), 75.15% (W) Target date: 2020-12-31 Target value: 92%

Base year: 2019 Base value: 76.19% (O), 75.15% (W) Target date: 2020-12-31 Target value: 92%
